aspect_notes: Flat lacustrine shoreline bench around Mono Lake; high salinity and pH 10 groundwater
secondary_plants: Ericameria nauseosa (Rubber rabbitbrush), Schoenoplectus acutus (Tule reeds at fresh springs)
ground_cover: White efflorescent trona salt crust, black volcanic beach sand, pumice pebbles, alkali fly pupae casings
rock_types: Calcium carbonate tufa towers, basaltic beach sand, rhyolitic pumice float
source: USFS Ecological Subsections M261E / Mono Basin Scenic Area

aspect_notes: Gently sloping southern and eastern basin floor; deep well-drained windblown volcanic tephra
dominant_plants: Artemisia tridentata ssp. wyomingensis (Wyoming big sagebrush), Purshia tridentata (Antelope bitterbrush)
secondary_plants: Chrysothamnus viscidiflorus (Yellow rabbitbrush), Prunus andersonii (Desert peach), Ephedra viridis (Mormon tea)
ground_cover: Loose pale grey-white pumice lapilli, obsidian flakes, sparse cheatgrass and Indian ricegrass
rock_types: Holocene rhyolite pumice, black obsidian dome talus, basaltic cinders (Black Point)
source: USGS Geologic Map I-1933 / LANDFIRE Biophysical Settings

aspect_notes: Glacial lateral moraines, alluvial fans, and Bodie Hills rolling slopes; all aspects
dominant_plants: Artemisia tridentata ssp. vaseyana (Mountain big sagebrush), Purshia tridentata
secondary_plants: Cercocarpus ledifolius (Curl-leaf mountain mahogany), Symphoricarpos oreophilus (Mountain snowberry)
ground_cover: Coarse granitic grus or volcanic gravel, needle litter, lupine, sulfur buckwheat
rock_types: Glacial till (mixed granodiorite erratics) on Sierra side; Miocene dacite/rhyolite breccia in Bodie Hills
source: LANDFIRE Inter-Mountain Basins Montane Sagebrush Steppe

aspect_notes: Dry south- and east-facing rocky fault scarps, Conway Summit slopes, and north shore hills
dominant_plants: Pinus monophylla (Single-leaf pinyon pine), Juniperus osteosperma (Utah juniper)
secondary_plants: Artemisia arbuscula (Low sagebrush), Cercocarpus ledifolius (Mountain mahogany)
ground_cover: Angular rock talus, dry pine needles, bare mineral soil patches, rock buckwheat
rock_types: Fractured hornfels, granodiorite outcrops, and weathered volcanic tuff
source: USFS Inyo NF Vegetation Map / Sawyer & Keeler-Wolf

aspect_notes: Perennial creek bottoms, canyon floors (Lee Vining, Lundy, Mill, DeChambeau creeks) and spring seeps
dominant_plants: Populus tremuloides (Quaking aspen), Populus trichocarpa (Black cottonwood)
secondary_plants: Salix exigua & Salix lutea (Narrowleaf and yellow willow), Betula occidentalis (Water birch), Rosa woodsii (Wild rose)
ground_cover: Thick dark humus, fallen golden/brown leaves, sedges, horsetail, water-rounded granite cobbles
rock_types: Stream-polished granodiorite boulders and alluvial gravel bars

aspect_notes: Cool north-facing moraine flanks, lower Lee Vining Canyon floor, and Mono Mills bench
secondary_plants: Abies concolor (White fir), Arctostaphylos patula (Greenleaf manzanita), Ceanothus velutinus (Tobacco brush)
ground_cover: Long pine-needle carpet, large pine cones, decomposing wood, pale granitic sand openings
rock_types: Cathedral Peak and Half Dome granodiorite boulders

aspect_notes: Upper Lee Vining Canyon, Ellery Lake, Tioga Lake, and Dana Meadows glaciated basins
dominant_plants: Pinus contorta ssp. murrayana (Sierra lodgepole pine), Pinus albicaulis (Whitebark pine)
secondary_plants: Tsuga mertensiana (Mountain hemlock on shady north benches), Salix orestera (Sierra willow), Vaccinium cespitosum
ground_cover: Moist sedge turf (Carex filifolia) in meadows; clean white granitic grus and slab bedrock on ridges
rock_types: Glacially polished Cathedral Peak granodiorite and metavolcanic contact hornfels

aspect_notes: Wind-scoured high ridges, Dana Plateau, and Mount Dana summit cone above treeline
dominant_plants: Pinus albicaulis (Prostrate krummholz mats at lower edge), Carex exserta (Shorthair sedge)
secondary_plants: Hulsea algida (Alpine gold), Polemonium eximium (Sky pilot), Eriogonum ovalifolium (Cushion buckwheat)
ground_cover: 90% angular boulder talus, frost-shattered scree, crustose lichens, and lingering neve snowfields
rock_types: Iron-stained Jurassic/Triassic metavolcanic breccia (Mount Dana) and pale granodiorite
source: NPS Yosemite Alpine Ecology / USGS GQ-154
